full_final_triples.relationship: overlapping prophetic dating by named kings
full_final_triples.rationale: Both openings place the prophetic words in the reigns of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash of Israel. Hosea also lists three additional Judean kings; Amos adds the earthquake dating.
full_final_triples.source_text: The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

target_units.text: The words of Amos that came among nakkarim from Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel portrayal of Israel's unfaithfulness as prostitution
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's commanded household sign explains the land's departure from the Lord as prostitution. Jeremiah likewise describes Israel's worship on mountains and beneath trees as prostitution and adultery with wood and stone.
full_final_triples.source_text: The beginning of the Lord’s word to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a woman of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land will utterly prostitute itself away from following the Lord.”

target_units.text: The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.
After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.

I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
Her prostitution came to be regarded as nothing, and she committed adultery with wood and stone.

full_final_triples.relationship: related prophetic births bearing announced national signs
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea takes Gomer, who bears a son; Isaiah approaches the prophetess, who likewise bears a son. The surrounding divine naming commands give both births a sign concerning national events.

Do not become drunk with wine, but associate with righteous people, and converse during walks; for if you give your eyes to bowls and cups, afterward you will walk about barer than a pestle.
But at the end he lies stretched out as though struck by a snake, and as though by a horned viper its poison spreads through him.
When your eyes see another woman, then your mouth will speak crooked things,

full_final_triples.relationship: specific parallel of divination employing a rod
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea condemns inquiry through signs and rods amid estrangement from God. Ezekiel describes Babylon's king tossing a rod, questioning carved images and inspecting a liver; both connect rods with divinatory inquiry.
full_final_triples.source_text: They inquired by signs, and by his rods they announced things to him; they were led astray by a spirit of prostitution and prostituted themselves away from their God.

target_units.text: For Babylon’s king will stand upon the ancient road, at the beginning of the two roads, to divine a divination, toss a rod, question the carved images and inspect a liver at his right.

full_final_triples.relationship: close mountain-and-tree setting for unfaithful worship
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes sacrifices on mountains and hills beneath named trees and connects them with prostitution. Jeremiah likewise portrays Israel's prostitution on every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree.
full_final_triples.source_text: On the mountaintops they sacrificed, and on the hills they offered sacrifice, beneath oak, poplar and a tree providing shade, because shelter is good. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

target_units.text: The Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, You saw what the dwelling of Israel did to Me. They went upon every high mountain and beneath every wooded tree and prostituted themselves there.

full_final_triples.relationship: related confrontation concerning adultery and one's own conduct
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea refuses to single out daughters and daughters-in-law while the men themselves mix with prostitutes and sacrifice with initiates. Paul asks the teacher who forbids adultery whether he commits it; the different arguments bring those addressed into examination of their own conduct.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will certainly not call your daughters to account when they prostitute themselves, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves mixed with prostitutes and sacrificed with initiates; the people who understood became entangled with a prostitute.

target_units.text: you then who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim that one must not steal, do you steal?
You who say that one must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

full_final_triples.relationship: close prohibition of entering Gilgal
full_final_triples.rationale: Both passages explicitly prohibit entering Gilgal. Hosea addresses Judah, while Amos's surrounding call addresses Israel's house. Their other destinations differ; Hosea's house of On is not silently identified with Amos's Bethel.
full_final_triples.source_text: But you, Israel, do not be ignorant; and Judah, do not enter Gilgal or go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.

target_units.text: Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath; for Gilgal will certainly be taken captive, and Bethel will be as though it did not exist.”

full_final_triples.relationship: related bovine images for Israel or Ephraim needing restraint
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares Israel to a heifer running wild. Jeremiah represents Ephraim as a calf not taught, speaking after discipline and asking to return; the shared animal image has different immediate developments.
full_final_triples.source_text: For Israel has run wild like a heifer running wild. Now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in an open place.

target_units.text: I surely heard Ephraim wailing: Thou didst discipline me, and I was disciplined; like a calf I was not taught. Turn me back, and I will return, because Thou art the Lord my God.

full_final_triples.relationship: close link between idols and a stumbling block
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea calls Ephraim a partner of idols who set stumbling blocks for himself. The psalm says service of carved images became a stumbling block to the people.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim, a partner of idols, set stumbling blocks for himself.

target_units.text: They served their carved images, and it became a stumbling block to them.

full_final_triples.relationship: related association with nations and prostitution through their practices
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea associates choosing Canaanites with prostitution and dishonor. The psalm describes mixing with nations, learning their works, serving Canaan's images and prostituting themselves through their practices.
full_final_triples.source_text: He chose Canaanites. They prostituted themselves thoroughly; they loved dishonor arising from their arrogance.

target_units.text: and mixed with the nations and learned their works.
They served their carved images, and it became a stumbling block to them.
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons,
and shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters whom they sacrificed to Canaan’s carved images; the land was murdered with blood,
and was defiled by their works, and they prostituted themselves through their practices.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel trapping imagery in accusations against the people
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea addresses priests, Israel and the royal house as a trap and stretched net. Jeremiah describes impious people setting traps to catch men and compares their deceitful houses to a bird-filled trap.
full_final_triples.source_text: Hear these things, priests; pay attention, house of Israel; listen, house of the king, for the judgment is against you. You became a trap at the lookout and like a net stretched over Itabyrion,

target_units.text: For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel divine knowledge of wrongdoing
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea declares that Ephraim is known and Israel is not away from God amid their defilement. Jeremiah similarly says all their ways are before God's eyes and their wrongdoings are not hidden.
full_final_triples.source_text: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not away from Me; for now Ephraim has prostituted himself and Israel is defiled.

target_units.text: Because My eyes are upon all their ways, and their wrongdoings were not hidden before My eyes.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel failure of unfaithful Israel to return
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says their schemes were not directed toward returning and associates this with a spirit of prostitution. Jeremiah likewise recounts Israel's prostitution followed by God's call to return and her failure to do so.
full_final_triples.source_text: They did not direct their schemes toward returning to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they did not recognize the Lord.

target_units.text: After she prostituted herself in all these ways, I said, Return to Me. But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her faithlessness.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel humbling of arrogance
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea announces Israel's arrogance humbled and the weakening of Israel, Ephraim and Judah. Isaiah likewise announces humbling for the insolent, arrogant and elevated on the Lord's day.
full_final_triples.source_text: Israel’s arrogance will be humbled before his face. Israel and Ephraim will weaken in their injustices, and Judah too will weaken with them.

target_units.text: For the Lord’s eyes are high, but the human being is low; humanity’s height will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
For the Lord Sabaoth has a day against every insolent and arrogant person, against everyone high and elevated; they will be humbled,

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel rejected approach accompanied by animal offerings
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says people will seek God with sheep and calves but not find Him because He turned away. Isaiah refuses abundant animal offerings and says God turns His eyes away from supplication amid bloodshed.
full_final_triples.source_text: With sheep and calves they will go to seek the Lord, but they will certainly not find Him, because He turned away from them,

target_units.text: “What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel trumpet warning amid approaching judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea commands a trumpet signal on the hills and proclamation in the house of On. Jeremiah similarly commands a trumpet over the land and urgent gathering and flight because crushing is coming from the north; the locations are distinct.
full_final_triples.source_text: Blow a trumpet on the hills; sound out on the heights; proclaim in the house of On! Benjamin was beside himself;

target_units.text: Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.

full_final_triples.relationship: legal counterpart to the image of moving boundaries
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares Judah's rulers to people moving boundaries. Deuteronomy expressly prohibits removing a neighbor's inherited boundaries, supplying a concrete legal counterpart to Hosea's accusation.
full_final_triples.source_text: Judah’s rulers became like people moving boundaries; upon them I will pour My onrush like water.

target_units.text: You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries, which your fathers set in your inheritance, which was allotted unto you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel human suppression of judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea charges Ephraim with oppressing his adversary and trampling judgment. Isaiah's confession likewise says, We drove judgment backward, and describes God's displeasure at the absence of judgment.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim oppressed his adversary and trampled judgment, because he began to follow worthless things.

target_units.text: We acted impiously and lied and withdrew from following our God. We spoke unjust things and disobeyed; we conceived and meditated on unjust words from our heart.
We drove judgment backward, and righteousness has withdrawn far away, for truth was consumed in their ways, and they could not go straight through.
Truth has been taken away, and they turned their mind away from understanding. The Lord saw, and it did not please Him that there was no judgment.

full_final_triples.relationship: related goad image in divine confrontation
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says God is like a goad to Judah's house. In Acts the voice identifying Himself as Jesus tells Saul that kicking against goads is hard; the shared image does not identify the two recipients or explain Hosea's separate turmoil clause.
full_final_triples.source_text: I am like turmoil to Ephraim and like a goad to Judah’s house.

target_units.text: When we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.’
I said, ‘Who art Thou, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

full_final_triples.relationship: later repudiation of the Assyrian help found inadequate earlier
full_final_triples.rationale: The earlier accusation says the Assyrian king could not heal Ephraim and Judah's pain. The later confession explicitly says Assur will not save; the repeated rejection of Assyrian rescue is expressed through different images.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim saw his illness and Judah his pain; Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent ambassadors to King Jarim. But he could not heal you, and pain will certainly not cease among you.

target_units.text: Assur will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse, and we will certainly no longer call the works of our hands “Our gods.” The One in you will have mercy on an orphan.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared predatory imagery with no rescuer
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares God to a panther and lion who seizes with no rescuer. Isaiah compares the approaching force to lions and describes seizing and an absence of rescue; the depicted agents differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: For I am like a panther to Ephraim and like a lion to Judah’s house. I seize and will go away and take, and there will be no one to rescue.

target_units.text: They rush like lions and have taken their stand like a lion’s cub. It will seize and cry out as a beast does and cast out, and no one will rescue them.

full_final_triples.relationship: close seeking and rising early toward God under affliction
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says they will seek God's face and rise early toward Him in affliction. The psalm says that whenever He killed them, they sought Him, returned and rose early toward God; Hosea's opening until-they-disappear clause is not rewritten as an admission of guilt.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will go and return to My place until they disappear; they will seek My face, and in their affliction they will rise early toward Me, saying,

target_units.text: Whenever He killed them, they sought Him; and they returned and rose early toward God,
and remembered that God is their helper, and God Most High is their redeemer.

full_final_triples.relationship: close pairing of divine striking and healing
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's call to return says God seized and will heal, and will strike and dress wounds. Eliphaz similarly says God causes pain and restores, struck and healed with His hands.
full_final_triples.source_text: “Let us go and return to the Lord our God, because He has seized us and will heal us; He will strike and dress our wounds.

target_units.text: Happy is the person whom the Lord reproved; do not refuse the Almighty’s admonition.
For He causes pain and restores again; He struck, and His hands healed.

full_final_triples.relationship: related third-day rising and life
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's collective voice expects restored health and rising to live before God on the third day. Paul's received proclamation says Christ was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures; the comparison distinguishes the communal promise from the named resurrection.
full_final_triples.source_text: He will restore us to health after two days; on the third day we will rise and live before Him.

target_units.text: For I handed over to you as matters of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
and that He was buried, and that He has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

full_final_triples.relationship: shared early-and-late rain language in renewed divine provision
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares God's coming to early and late rain as the people pursue knowledge of Him. Joel promises early and late rainfall to Zion's children; it describes rainfall itself rather than repeating Hosea's comparison of God to rain.
full_final_triples.source_text: We will know; we will pursue knowledge of the Lord. We will find Him ready like dawn, and He will come to us like rain, early and late upon the land.”

target_units.text: Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because He gave you food for righteousness, and He will rain upon you early and late rainfall as before.

full_final_triples.relationship: internal recurrence of the vanishing cloud-and-dew image
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea first compares the people's mercy to a morning cloud and passing dew. The later judgment applies the same two images to the people themselves, changing the object of the comparison while retaining its transience.
full_final_triples.source_text: What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away.

target_units.text: Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away, like chaff blown from a threshing floor and like vapor from locusts.

full_final_triples.relationship: related lethal force of divinely spoken words
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says God killed the prophets with His mouth's words. Jeremiah depicts God's words in the prophet's mouth as fire consuming the people as wood; the recipients and the mouth through which the words act are distinct.
full_final_triples.source_text: Therefore I mowed down your prophets; I killed them with the words of My mouth, and My judgment will go forth like light.

target_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Almighty: Because you spoke this utterance, behold, I have made My words fire in your mouth, and this people wood, and it will devour them.

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit quotation concerning mercy toward sinners
full_final_triples.rationale: Jesus quotes Hosea's preference for mercy over sacrifice when answering criticism of His eating with tax collectors and sinners. Matthew gives the mercy clause, while Hosea also expressly prefers knowledge of God to whole burnt offerings.
full_final_triples.source_text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.

target_units.text: Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit quotation against condemning the guiltless
full_final_triples.rationale: Jesus again uses Hosea's mercy-over-sacrifice words in the dispute over His disciples plucking grain on the Sabbath. This application specifically rebukes condemning the guiltless, a distinct setting from Matthew 9.
full_final_triples.source_text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.

target_units.text: If you had known what ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice’ means, you would not have condemned the guiltless.

full_final_triples.relationship: related defilement of both sister communities
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea links Ephraim's prostitution with Israel and Judah being defiled. Ezekiel's two women, identified in the context as Samaria and Jerusalem, share a way of defilement, with Oholibah's corruption exceeding her sister's.
full_final_triples.source_text: In Israel’s house I saw dreadful things, there Ephraim’s prostitution; Israel and Judah were defiled.

target_units.text: Her sister Oholibah saw this and corrupted her desire beyond hers, and her prostitution beyond her sister’s prostitution.
She set her desire upon Assyrians’ sons, leaders and generals near her, clothed in finely bordered garments, horsemen riding horses; all choice young men.
I saw that she was defiled; one way for the two.

full_final_triples.relationship: related harvest language joined to reversal of captivity
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea commands harvesting when God turns back His people's captivity. The psalm asks for captivity to be turned back and describes sowers returning with sheaves and exultation.
full_final_triples.source_text: Begin harvesting for yourself when I turn back My people’s captivity,

target_units.text: Turn back our captivity, Lord, like torrents in the south.
Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.
Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.

full_final_triples.relationship: specific roadside stripping by robbers
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea includes a robber stripping someone on his road in the exposure of injustice. Jesus' parable describes robbers stripping a traveler on the Jerusalem-Jericho road; the comparison concerns the concrete assault, without equating the two settings.
full_final_triples.source_text: when I heal Israel. Ephraim’s injustice and Samaria’s wickedness will be uncovered, because they practiced falsehood. A thief will enter upon him, a robber stripping him on his road,

target_units.text: Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.

full_final_triples.relationship: close placement of wrongs before God's face
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says God remembered their evils and that their schemes came before His face. The psalm likewise says their lawless deeds were set before God and their age is in His face's light.
full_final_triples.source_text: so that they sing together as people singing together with their heart. I remembered all their evils; now their schemes have surrounded them; they have come before My face.

target_units.text: Thou didst set our lawless deeds before Thee; our age is in the light of Thy face.

full_final_triples.relationship: related royal receptiveness to wrongdoing
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea charges that evils gladdened kings and falsehoods gladdened rulers. Proverbs describes a king listening to an unjust word and lawlessness among those under him; both connect corrupt speech and conduct with the royal setting.
full_final_triples.source_text: With their evils they gladdened kings, and with their falsehoods, rulers.

target_units.text: When a king listens to an unjust word, all those under him are lawless.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel collective adultery expressed through vivid appetite imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea calls all of them adulterers and compares them to a burning oven. Jeremiah likewise describes adultery and prostitutes' houses, comparing the men to horses longing for their neighbors' wives; the figurative vehicles differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: All are adulterers, like an oven burning for the baking of something scorched by flame, from the kneading of fat until it ferments.

target_units.text: For which of these things should I be merciful to you? Your sons abandoned Me and swore by those who are not gods. And I fed them fully, and they committed adultery and lodged in prostitutes’ houses.
They became horses mad for mares; each neighed after his neighbor’s wife.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel disorder among leaders associated with wine
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes rulers raging from wine on the kings' days. Isaiah describes priest and prophet losing their senses and reeling through wine and sikera; the affected offices and particular actions differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: On your kings’ days the rulers began to rage from wine; he stretched out his hand with pestilent men,

target_units.text: For these have been led astray by wine and wandered because of sikera. Priest and prophet lost their senses because of wine, reeled from sikera’s intoxication and went astray. This is an apparition.

full_final_triples.relationship: same-chapter development of the heated oven image
full_final_triples.rationale: The earlier verse depicts the adulterers as a burning oven. This verse returns to the oven image for their kindled hearts while they batter people, adding overnight sleep and morning blaze to the comparison.
full_final_triples.source_text: because their hearts were kindled like an oven as they battered people. All night Ephraim was filled with sleep; morning came, and he was kindled like fire’s blaze.

target_units.text: All are adulterers, like an oven burning for the baking of something scorched by flame, from the kneading of fat until it ferments.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel failure to recognize destructive losses
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says foreigners consumed Ephraim's strength without his recognizing it. Isaiah describes Israel being plundered and overpowered by war and burning without understanding or taking it to soul.
full_final_triples.source_text: Foreigners devoured his strength, but he did not recognize it; gray hairs blossomed upon him, but he did not know it.

target_units.text: Who gave Jacob over to plunder and Israel to those despoiling him? Was it not God, against whom they sinned, refusing to walk in His ways or listen to His law?
He brought His wrathful anger upon them; war overpowered them, as did those burning them all around. None of them understood, nor did they take it to soul.

full_final_triples.relationship: close refusal to return despite affliction
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says Israel did not return to God or seek Him amid these things. Amos repeatedly describes blows and devastation followed by the charge that even so the people did not turn to Him.
full_final_triples.source_text: Israel’s arrogance will be humbled before his face, yet they did not return to the Lord their God or seek Him in all these things.

target_units.text: “I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

“I sent death among you on Egypt’s road and killed your young men with the sword, along with the captivity of your horses. I brought your camps up in fire in My anger; yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.
“I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched from fire. Yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

full_final_triples.relationship: related unwise appeal to Egypt for help
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea depicts Ephraim as a senseless dove calling on Egypt and going to the Assyrians. Isaiah condemns going to Egypt without asking God and says Pharaoh's shelter becomes shame; the Egyptian appeal is shared, while Hosea also names Assyria.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim was like a senseless dove without understanding; he called on Egypt, and they went to the Assyrians.

target_units.text: “Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,
you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.

full_final_triples.relationship: close divine net spread over those facing judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says God will cast His net over them and bring them down like birds. Ezekiel likewise promises God's net over the ruler and captivity in Babylon; the recipients and accompanying images differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: Whenever they go, I will cast My net over them; I will bring them down like heaven’s birds. I will discipline them when their affliction is heard.

target_units.text: I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My enclosure. I will bring him to Babylon, to the Chaldeans’ land, and he will not see it, and there he will die.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel accusation of speaking falsely against the Lord
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea contrasts God's redemption with their falsehoods against Him. Jeremiah likewise says they lied to their own Lord and denied that sword or famine would come; it specifies the false speech differently.
full_final_triples.source_text: Woe to them, because they sprang away from Me! They are miserable, because they acted impiously toward Me. I redeemed them, but they spoke falsehoods against Me.

target_units.text: They lied to their own Lord and said: These things are not so; evils will not come upon us, and we will not see sword or famine.

full_final_triples.relationship: related self-cutting within failed religious appeals
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea contrasts lack of heartfelt crying to God with howling and cutting themselves over grain and wine. Kings depicts Baal's prophets calling and cutting themselves without an answering voice; Hosea does not identify its participants as that particular group.
full_final_triples.source_text: Their hearts did not cry to Me; they only howled on their beds. They cut themselves over grain and wine. They were disciplined through Me,

target_units.text: They took the young bull and prepared it. They called on Baal’s name from morning until noon, saying, “Hear us, Baal, hear us!” But there was no voice and no hearing. They ran about on the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, “Call with a loud voice, for he is a god! He has chattering to do; perhaps he is also conducting business, or perhaps he is asleep and will get up!”
They called with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with knives and lances, until blood poured over them.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared turning-away and bow imagery with different descriptions
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says they turned toward nothing and became like a drawn bow. The psalm joins turning back and breaking faith with becoming a crooked bow; its crooked description must not replace Hosea's drawn bow.
full_final_triples.source_text: They turned away toward nothing; they became like a drawn bow. Their rulers will fall by the sword because of their tongues’ lack of discipline. This is their contempt in Egypt’s land.

target_units.text: and turned back and broke faith just like their fathers, and changed into a crooked bow,

full_final_triples.relationship: related eagle image for threatening approach
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea places an eagle against the Lord's house in an accusation of covenant and law transgression. Deuteronomy warns of a distant nation coming like an eagle's swoop; the comparison does not resolve Hosea's unusual opening bosom-and-earth phrase.
full_final_triples.source_text: Into their bosom like earth, like an eagle against the Lord’s house, because they transgressed My covenant and acted impiously against My law.

target_units.text: The Lord shall bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, as the swooping of an eagle, a nation whose speech you shall not understand,

full_final_triples.relationship: related claimed relationship accompanied by rejected lawlessness
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea gives the cry, God, we know Thee, within the covenant-breaking accusation. Matthew contrasts calling Lord, Lord with the rejection of those practicing lawlessness and the declaration I never knew you; the direction of the knowing claim differs.
full_final_triples.source_text: They will cry to Me, ‘God, we know Thee!’

target_units.text: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of My Father in the heavens.
Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Thy name, cast out demons in Thy name, and do many mighty works in Thy name?’
Then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness.’

full_final_triples.relationship: concrete parallel of precious metal fashioned into an idol
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea charges that the people made silver and gold into idols. Exodus narrates gold earrings received by Aaron and fashioned into a cast calf; it supplies a concrete instance without identifying it as Hosea's later calf.
full_final_triples.source_text: They reigned for themselves and not through Me; they ruled and did not make it known to Me. They made their silver and gold into idols for themselves, so that they might be destroyed.

target_units.text: Aaron said to them, “Take off the gold earrings from the ears of your wives and daughters, and bring them to me.”
All the people took off the gold earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He received them from their hands, fashioned them with an engraving tool, and made them into a cast calf. He said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”

full_final_triples.relationship: related angry rejection of a calf image
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea commands Samaria to rub away its calf and declares God's provoked anger. Exodus records Moses' anger and destruction of the calf; the commands, agents and procedures are distinct.
full_final_triples.source_text: Rub away your calf, Samaria! My anger was provoked against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed

target_units.text: As he approached the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. In his anger Moses threw the two tablets from his hands and shattered them at the mountain’s foot.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it fine, scattered it on the water, and made the sons of Israel drink it.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel rejection of human-made objects as divine powers
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says a craftsman made the calf and it is no god. Jeremiah describes carpentry and metal decoration producing objects that must be carried and cannot provide good; both expose the dependence of the worshipped objects on makers.
full_final_triples.source_text: in Israel? A craftsman made it, and it is no god, because your calf was leading people astray, Samaria.

target_units.text: For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.
They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.
They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.

full_final_triples.relationship: close threat of foreigners consuming the harvest
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says even flour from the weak sheaf will be consumed by foreigners. Deuteronomy likewise threatens an unknown nation consuming the land's yield and all the people's labor; Hosea's opening wind-blasted sowing is not recast as a whirlwind.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because they sowed wind-blasted things, their overthrow will receive them: a sheaf without strength to make flour. Even if it does make flour, foreigners will devour it.

target_units.text: A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.

full_final_triples.relationship: close useless-vessel image for rejection and displacement
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea depicts Israel among the nations as a useless vessel. Jeremiah describes Jeconiah as a vessel of no use, cast into an unknown land; the collective people and named individual remain distinct.
full_final_triples.source_text: Israel was swallowed up; now he became among the nations like a useless vessel.

target_units.text: Jeconiah was dishonored like a vessel for which there is no use, because he was cast out and thrown into a land he did not know.

full_final_triples.relationship: internal recurrence of Assyrian diplomacy
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea first describes going to the Assyrians and loving gifts. The later accusation explicitly names an Assyrian covenant and trade with Egypt; it develops the recurring foreign-relations theme without turning Ephraim's flourishing into a wild-ass image.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because they went up to the Assyrians; Ephraim flourished by himself, and they loved gifts.

target_units.text: But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued scorching heat all day, multiplied empty and worthless things, made a covenant with the Assyrians, and traded oil into Egypt.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel multiplication of altars within condemned worship
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says multiplying altars produced occasions of sin for Ephraim. Jeremiah describes altars for Baal corresponding to Jerusalem's exits and gods as numerous as Judah's cities, another accusation of proliferating worship sites.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because Ephraim multiplied altars, beloved altars became occasions of sin for him.

target_units.text: For your gods were according to the number of your cities, Judah; and according to the number of Jerusalem’s exits you set up altars to burn incense to Baal.

full_final_triples.relationship: close rejection of sacrifice amid disobedience
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says sacrifices and meat will not secure God's acceptance and announces remembrance of sins. Jeremiah likewise rejects whole burnt offerings and sacrifices after charging rejection of God's word and law.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because even if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them. Now He will remember their injustices and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among the Assyrians.

target_units.text: Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.
Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.

full_final_triples.relationship: close announced fire devouring urban foundations
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea mentions Judah's multiplied walled cities and announces fire devouring foundations. Amos likewise announces fire upon Judah that will devour Jerusalem's foundations, after charging rejection of God's law.
full_final_triples.source_text: Israel forgot his Maker, and they built sacred precincts; Judah multiplied walled cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of the sons of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they rejected the Lord’s law and did not keep His ordinances. Their vain things, which they made, led them astray—the things their fathers followed.
I will send fire upon Judah, and it will devour Jerusalem’s foundations.”

full_final_triples.relationship: internal relation between prostitution imagery and desired provision
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea condemns loving gifts at grain threshing floors while prostituting oneself away from God. The earlier woman likewise says she will follow lovers whom she credits with bread and other necessities; both join unfaithfulness with desired material provision.
full_final_triples.source_text: Do not rejoice, Israel, or be glad like the peoples, because you prostituted yourself away from your God; you loved gifts on every threshing floor of grain.

target_units.text: For their mother prostituted herself; she who bore them brought shame. She said, ‘I will follow my lovers, who give me my loaves and water, my garments and linen cloths, my oil and everything due to me.’

full_final_triples.relationship: close prediction of eating unclean things among foreign peoples
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea names eating unclean things among the Assyrians. Ezekiel's food-sign instruction likewise announces that Israel's sons will eat unclean things among the nations, without naming Assyria in that unit.
full_final_triples.source_text: They did not dwell in the Lord’s land; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.

target_units.text: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: So the sons of Israel will eat unclean things among the nations.’”

full_final_triples.relationship: related mourning, food and ritual uncleanness
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares the sacrifices to defiling bread of mourning, excluded from the Lord's house. Deuteronomy's tithe declaration expressly denies eating the holy produce in mourning or offering it for an unclean use; the legal and judgment settings differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: They did not pour wine to the Lord or make it pleasant to Him. Their sacrifices are like bread of mourning to them; all who eat them will be defiled, because their loaves for their own lives will not enter the Lord’s house.

target_units.text: And I have not eaten thereof in my mourning, neither have I offered thereof for an unclean use, nor given thereof unto the dead. I have hearkened unto the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel thorns in human habitations under judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's announcement of departure and burial includes thorns in the people's dwellings. Isaiah likewise describes thorny trees sprouting in cities and fortifications; the named places and other judgments differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: Therefore look, they will go away from Egypt’s misery; Memphis will receive them, and Machmas will bury them. Destruction will inherit their silver; thorns will be in their dwellings.

target_units.text: Thorny trees will sprout in their cities and her fortifications; she will become a dwelling for sirens and a courtyard for ostriches.

full_final_triples.relationship: close phrase days of vengeance in announced calamity
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea announces that the days of vengeance and repayment have come. Luke calls the impending days around Jerusalem days of vengeance for what is written to be fulfilled; this is a verbal and judgment-setting comparison, not an equation of the events.
full_final_triples.source_text: The days of vengeance have come; the days of your repayment have come. Israel will be afflicted like the deranged prophet, a spirit-bearing man. Because your injustices were many, your madness increased.

target_units.text: because these are days of vengeance, for all that is written to be fulfilled.

full_final_triples.relationship: related prophetic watchman language with contrasting duties and danger
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea places Ephraim's watchman with God and then describes a prophet as a crooked trap. Ezekiel appoints the son of man as Israel's watchman to convey God's warning; the comparison preserves Hosea's distinct clauses rather than merging their figures.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim’s watchman is with God; a prophet, a crooked trap upon all his ways. They fixed madness in the Lord’s house.

target_units.text: “Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. You will hear a word from My mouth and convey My warning to them.

full_final_triples.relationship: internal repeated announcement of remembering and punishing sins
full_final_triples.rationale: Both passages announce God's remembrance of injustices and punishment of sins. Hosea 9 adds corruption as in the hill's days; this comparison does not assign that unnamed reference to a particular historical incident.
full_final_triples.source_text: They were corrupted as in the hill’s days. He will remember his injustices; He will punish his sins.

target_units.text: Because even if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them. Now He will remember their injustices and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among the Assyrians.

full_final_triples.relationship: related account of Israel's attachment to the Peor cult
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea recalls Israel's going to Beel-phegor and becoming estranged into shame. Numbers narrates Israel's participation in sacrifices and initiation into worship called Baal of Peor; the native forms of the cult name are preserved.
full_final_triples.source_text: Like a cluster of grapes in a wilderness I found Israel, and like an early lookout in a fig tree I saw their fathers. They went to Beel-phegor and became estranged into shame, and the beloved became like the detested.

target_units.text: And Israel lodged at Shittim, and the people profaned themselves by engaging in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
And they invited them to the sacrifices of their idols. The people ate from their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols.
And Israel was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor, and the Lord became angry with Israel.

full_final_triples.relationship: related threatened loss of children
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says that even rearing children will end in bereavement. Deuteronomy describes sons and daughters given to another nation while their parents watch helplessly; these are distinct forms of parental loss, without explaining Hosea's separate My-flesh clause.
full_final_triples.source_text: because even if they rear their children, they will be bereaved among humankind. Indeed, woe is upon them: My flesh is from them.

target_units.text: Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.

full_final_triples.relationship: close barren-womb and unnourishing-breast language under calamity
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea asks for a childless womb and dry breasts. Jesus predicts days when people will call the barren, wombs that did not bear and breasts that did not nourish blessed; the request and future saying differ within their respective judgment settings.
full_final_triples.source_text: Give them, Lord—what wilt Thou give them? Give them a childless womb and dry breasts.

target_units.text: For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nourish.’

full_final_triples.relationship: related divine rejection of house and inheritance
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea announces hatred at Gilgal, expulsion from God's house and an end to love. Jeremiah likewise speaks of abandoning God's house and hating the inheritance that raised its voice against Him; the descriptions of rejection differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: All their evils are at Gilgal, because there I hated them. Because of their wicked practices I will expel them from My house. I will certainly love them no longer; all their rulers are disobedient.

target_units.text: I have abandoned My house, let go My inheritance, and given My beloved soul into her enemies’ hands.
My inheritance became to Me like a lion in woodland; she raised her voice against Me, therefore I hated her.

full_final_triples.relationship: close dried-root image for destructive judgment
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes Ephraim dried at the roots and unable to bear fruit. Bildad likewise describes roots drying below and harvest falling above; the shared plant image does not make his depicted individual identical with Ephraim.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim suffered; he dried up at his roots; he will certainly bear fruit no longer. Even if they give birth, I will kill the desired offspring of their womb.

target_units.text: Below, his roots will dry up; above, his harvest will fall.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel displacement among nations without settled rest
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea predicts rejection for not listening and wandering among the nations. Deuteronomy likewise describes scattering among all nations and no resting place for the foot within its warnings for disobedience.
full_final_triples.source_text: God will thrust them away because they did not listen to Him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.

target_units.text: And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

And among those nations He shall give you no rest, neither shall there be a resting place for the sole of your foot; and the Lord shall give you there a faint heart, and failing eyes, and a wasting soul.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel identification of Israel through vine or vineyard imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea portrays Israel as a luxuriant, fruitful vine whose abundance accompanies multiplied altars. Isaiah identifies the Lord's vineyard as Israel's house and contrasts expected judgment with lawlessness; Hosea's thriving fruit is not changed into Isaiah's failed moral yield.
full_final_triples.source_text: Israel is a vine with luxuriant branches, its fruit thriving. According to the abundance of his fruits he multiplied altars; according to his land’s good things he built pillars.

target_units.text: For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.

full_final_triples.relationship: related challenge to divided religious allegiance
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says they divided their hearts and announces destruction of altars and pillars. Elijah asks how long the people will limp on both knees and sets following the Lord against following Baal; the heart and knee images differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: They divided their hearts; now they will disappear. He will demolish their altars, and their pillars will suffer devastation.

target_units.text: Elijah came near them all and said to them, “How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, follow Him; if Baal is, follow him.” The people did not answer a word.

full_final_triples.relationship: related questioning of reliance on rulers
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's people ask what a king can do for them after failing to fear the Lord. The psalm warns against trust in rulers who have no salvation and instead commends hope in the Lord.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because now they will say, ‘We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord; and the king—what will he do for us?’

target_units.text: Do not trust in rulers and in sons of men who have no salvation.
His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their reasonings will perish.
Happy the one whose Helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God,

full_final_triples.relationship: related bound cult images carried away
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes the object bound and carried to the Assyrians as a gift for King Jarim. Isaiah likewise describes named carved images bound as burdens and led captive; the names, destinations and gift setting are not equated.
full_final_triples.source_text: They bound it and carried it to the Assyrians as guest-gifts for King Jarim. He will receive Ephraim as a gift, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.

target_units.text: Bel fell; Dagon was shattered. Their carved images became a burden for wild and domestic animals. Lift them, bound together, as a load for one who is weary
and hungry and exhausted, without strength at all; they cannot be saved from war, and they themselves were led captive.

full_final_triples.relationship: close mountain-and-hill appeal with the commands reversed
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea gives the appeals to mountains to cover and hills to fall upon the people. Jesus predicts appeals to mountains to fall and hills to cover; the distinctive paired appeals correspond while the assigned commands are reversed.
full_final_triples.source_text: The shrines of On, Israel’s sins, will be removed; thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us!’ and to the hills, ‘Fall upon us!’

target_units.text: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall upon us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’

full_final_triples.relationship: related calf imagery for Ephraim with different training descriptions
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea calls Ephraim a heifer trained to love strife. Jeremiah's Ephraim describes himself as a calf not taught and speaks of God's discipline; the contrast preserves strife rather than substituting threshing for Hosea's wording.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim is a heifer trained to love strife, but I will come upon the finest part of her neck. I will mount Ephraim and pass over Judah in silence; Jacob will strengthen him.

target_units.text: I surely heard Ephraim wailing: Thou didst discipline me, and I was disciplined; like a calf I was not taught. Turn me back, and I will return, because Thou art the Lord my God.

full_final_triples.relationship: close moral sowing and reaping of life
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea commands sowing in righteousness and reaping life's fruit. Galatians describes sowing into the Spirit and reaping eternal life, encouraging perseverance in good; the descriptions of the sowing are distinct.
full_final_triples.source_text: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap life’s fruit. Shine a light of knowledge for yourselves; seek the Lord until produce of righteousness comes to you.

target_units.text: For the one who sows into his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in the proper season we will reap, if we do not give up.

full_final_triples.relationship: shared sowing and fruit-of-righteousness imagery
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea links righteous sowing and the arrival of produce of righteousness with seeking God. James describes a fruit of righteousness sown in peace for peacemakers, adding a particular peace-making setting to the cultivation image.
full_final_triples.source_text: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap life’s fruit. Shine a light of knowledge for yourselves; seek the Lord until produce of righteousness comes to you.

target_units.text: And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.

full_final_triples.relationship: related eating of the consequences of one's wrong way
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes reaping injustices and eating false fruit amid reliance on chariots and force. Wisdom in Proverbs says the rejecters of her counsel will eat their own way's fruits and be filled with their ungodliness.
full_final_triples.source_text: Why did you pass over impiety in silence and reap its injustices, eating false fruit? Because you hoped in your chariots, in the multitude of your force.

target_units.text: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.

full_final_triples.relationship: related wartime violence against mothers and children
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea describes a mother dashed upon children in days of war. Elisha predicts Hazael's burning of strongholds, dashing of infants and tearing of pregnant women; the atrocities are compared without identifying Hazael with Hosea's Salaman.
full_final_triples.source_text: Destruction will arise among your people, and all your walled places will vanish. As the ruler Salaman from the house of Jerobaal, in days of war they dashed a mother to the ground upon children.

target_units.text: Hazael said, ‘Why does my lord weep?’ He said, ‘Because I know all the evils you will do to the sons of Israel: you will send their strongholds into fire, kill their chosen men with the sword, dash down their infants, and tear open their pregnant women.’

full_final_triples.relationship: internal recurrence of judgment against Israel's royal rule
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea's opening announces an end to the kingdom of Israel's house. The later declaration says Israel's king was cast off because of the people's evils; it does not name that king or equate the announcements' precise timing.
full_final_triples.source_text: So I will do to you, house of Israel, because of your evils. At dawn they were cast off; Israel’s king was cast off.

target_units.text: The Lord said to him, “Call him Jezreel, for in a little while I will avenge Jezreel’s blood upon Jehu’s house and put an end to the kingdom of Israel’s house.

full_final_triples.relationship: explicit fulfillment citation with a changed filial formulation
full_final_triples.rationale: Matthew applies an Egypt saying to the Child's stay there and quotes My Son. The supplied Hosea text instead says God loved infant Israel and summoned his children from Egypt; the plural and possessive difference is preserved.
full_final_triples.source_text: Because Israel was an infant, I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned his children.

target_units.text: He remained there until Herod’s death, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called My Son.”

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel divine approach answered by disobedience and illicit worship
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea contrasts God's summoning with departure, Baal sacrifices and incense to images. Isaiah describes God's outstretched hands to a disobedient people who provoke Him with sacrifices and incense; the described worship sites differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: As I summoned them, so they departed from My presence; they sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved images.

target_units.text: I spread out My hands all day to a disobedient, contradicting people who did not walk in a true way but followed their sins.
This people continually provokes Me to My face. They sacrifice in gardens and burn incense on bricks to demons that do not exist,

full_final_triples.relationship: related divine carrying and care from early life
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says God bound Ephraim's feet, took him upon His arm and healed without being recognized. Isaiah addresses Israel as carried from the belly and promises to take them up and save them; Hosea's binding is not rewritten as teaching to walk.
full_final_triples.source_text: I bound Ephraim’s feet together; I took him up on My arm, but they did not know that I have healed them.

target_units.text: “Listen to Me, house of Jacob and all Israel’s remnant, you who are carried from the belly and instructed from childhood.
Until old age I am, and until you grow very old I am. I bear with you; I made you, and I will release you. I will take you up and save you.

full_final_triples.relationship: internal pairing of Egypt and Assyria in Ephraim's condition
full_final_triples.rationale: Both passages state that Ephraim dwelt in Egypt and also speak of Assyria. The earlier passage adds unclean eating among Assyrians; the later calls Assur his king and names refusal to return, without specifying one shared historical episode.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and Assur himself was his king, because he did not wish to return.

target_units.text: They did not dwell in the Lord’s land; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.

full_final_triples.relationship: related eating from one's own wrongful course
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says they will eat from their schemes. Wisdom's warning says her rejecters will eat the fruits of their own way; the comparison concerns that consequence image and does not resolve Hosea's preceding weakened-sword clauses.
full_final_triples.source_text: A sword grew weak in his cities and ceased in his hands, and they will eat from their schemes.

target_units.text: Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.

full_final_triples.relationship: named city-overthrow precedent contrasted with hesitation to destroy
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea asks about making Israel like Adama and Seboim and describes God's stirred change of mind. Deuteronomy names Admah and Zeboiim among cities the Lord overthrew in anger; the native name forms and the contrasting responses are preserved.
full_final_triples.source_text: How shall I deal with you, Ephraim? Shall I shield you, Israel? How shall I deal with you? Shall I make you like Adama and like Seboim? My heart turned within itself; My change of mind was stirred together.

target_units.text: sulfur and salt, burned over; all its land shall neither be sown nor sprout, neither shall any green thing grow upon it, as at the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in wrath and anger—

full_final_triples.relationship: close assertion that God is not a human being
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea grounds the refusal to erase Ephraim in God's being God rather than human. Numbers likewise says God is not as a human to be led astray or threatened and asks whether His speech will be fulfilled; its particular predicates differ.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will certainly not act according to My furious anger; I will certainly not abandon Ephraim to be erased. For I am God and not a human being, holy within you, and I will not enter a city.

target_units.text: God is not as a man, to be led astray, nor as a son of man, to be threatened; having spoken, shall He not act? Shall He speak, and not abide by it?

full_final_triples.relationship: related roaring-lion imagery joined to response to God
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says the Lord will roar like a lion and describes children of waters being astonished. Amos pairs a lion's roar and fear with the Lord's speech and prophecy; it does not directly repeat Hosea's description of the Lord roaring.
full_final_triples.source_text: I will walk after the Lord. He will roar like a lion, because He Himself will howl, and children of waters will be astonished.

target_units.text: A lion will roar—and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken—and who will not prophesy?

full_final_triples.relationship: close restoration from both Egypt and Assyria
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea compares those from Egypt and Assyria to birds and promises restored houses. Isaiah likewise gathers those lost in Assyria and Egypt to worship the Lord in Jerusalem; its trumpet and destination differ from Hosea's details.
full_final_triples.source_text: They will be astonished like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the Assyrians’ land, and I will restore them to their houses, says the Lord.

target_units.text: On that day they will sound the great trumpet. Those lost in the Assyrians’ country and those lost in Egypt will come and bow to the Lord upon the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

full_final_triples.relationship: parallel accusation of Israel and Judah's rejection and falsehood
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea names Ephraim's falsehood and impieties involving Israel's house and Judah. Jeremiah likewise charges both houses with rejection and lying to their Lord; the comparison concerns these accusations, not Hosea's subsequent holy-people naming.
full_final_triples.source_text: Ephraim surrounded Me with falsehood, and Israel’s house and Judah with impieties. Now God knew them, and he will be called God’s holy people.

target_units.text: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have utterly rejected Me, says the Lord.
They lied to their own Lord and said: These things are not so; evils will not come upon us, and we will not see sword or famine.

full_final_triples.relationship: related foreign agreements involving Egypt without fidelity to God
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea condemns an Assyrian covenant and oil trade into Egypt. Isaiah condemns agreements made without God's spirit and going to Egypt without asking Him; the specific partners and transactions remain different.
full_final_triples.source_text: But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued scorching heat all day, multiplied empty and worthless things, made a covenant with the Assyrians, and traded oil into Egypt.

target_units.text: “Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,
you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.

full_final_triples.relationship: close divine repayment according to ways and practices
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea announces repayment to Jacob according to his ways and practices. Jeremiah likewise describes the Lord giving each person according to ways and the fruits of practices, after examining hearts and kidneys.
full_final_triples.source_text: The Lord has a case against Judah, to exact punishment on Jacob according to his ways; He will repay him according to his practices.

target_units.text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.

full_final_triples.relationship: related account of Jacob and his brother at birth
full_final_triples.rationale: Hosea says he tripped his brother in the womb. Genesis narrates Jacob emerging with his hand holding Esau's heel; the connection preserves the differing location and action instead of treating the wording as identical.
